title: Warm dust limits the spatial mixing of cold ice in the tested Gaia20cdd models
abstract: We convert the reported warm excess of Gaia20cdd into a spatial limit on cold ice. We use pure-ice absorption, stellar heating, vacuum sublimation and isotropic warm emission. For 0.1 um ice with an initial radius erosion time of at least 61 days, a 550 K warm spectrum requires an effective separation of 0.83 au for the single-star model or 0.89 au for the binary alternative. At most 1.46 or 1.27 percent of that warm luminosity can lie within 0.1 au of an ice grain. A positive-source bound extends the result to arbitrary spatial distributions with the same spectrum. Both populations can still share a broad orbital region. The full sensitivity grid gives 0.58-1.34 au at this ice size and time. Using only two measured infrared bins, with a stated within-bin shape, gives weaker limits near 0.2 au. The spectral shape, ice composition, transparent paths and selected erosion time are assumptions. This is a conditional model result, not a measured distance or grain lifetime. Code, source hashes, aggregate tables, checks and a retrieval recipe are included.
